sketch.alt: ZIMA-CAD Sketcher displaying a circle with a 9 mm radius dimension, the geometry tree, view controls, and OK and Cancel actions.

markers.title: Circle and centre
markers.body: The white circle is the sketch curve. Its white centre point is separate from the brown sketch origin at the lower left.

markers.title: Edit the radius
markers.body: Double-click the displayed R9mm dimension to open its value editor. The same radius dimension is listed under Dimensions in the tree.

markers.title: Look normal to the sketch
markers.body: Normal view aligns the camera with the Sketch plane. The two following controls both read Flip: the first switches front/back, the second rotates the view in 90° steps.

markers.title: Finish the edit
markers.body: OK finishes Sketch editing. An embedded Sketch returns its draft to the owning operation's Properties, which also need confirmation. Cancel below discards this session's edits.

feature.alt: ZIMA-CAD Feature Properties for an extrusion with empty placement references, XY plane, Sketch, Add and Subtract, and OK and Cancel.

markers.title: Place the feature
markers.body: Click the reference field to arm geometry selection. The eye in the same row is a separate inspection control. This capture has no placement reference entered.

markers.title: Define the profile
markers.body: Click Sketch to edit the feature profile. XY is currently selected in the plane controls to the left; the plane offset reads 0,000 mm.

markers.title: Choose the material operation
markers.body: Add adds material; Subtract removes it. Add is selected here, with Body as the result type.

markers.title: Confirm the complete definition
markers.body: After defining the profile and limits, click OK to validate and calculate the feature. Cancel discards the pending dialog changes. The capture shows the initial dialog, not a completed solid.

fillet-chamfer.alt: ZIMA-CAD solid Fillet Properties with a 1 mm constant radius, three selected input-body edges and their cyan wire feedback.

markers.title: Set the radius
markers.body: Edit Radius R to set the fillet radius. The displayed definition uses the Constant type and a radius of 1,000 mm.

markers.title: Add an edge reference
markers.body: Click Select reference, then select an input edge in the view. Three references are already listed; each red cross removes its corresponding list item.

markers.title: Check the selected edges
markers.body: Cyan wire feedback identifies the selected edges on the real input part. The dialog is still open, so this view must not be read as the committed final fillet result.

markers.title: Calculate and confirm
markers.body: Click OK to calculate and confirm the pending fillet. Cancel closes the dialog without committing its changes.

sheet-metal.alt: ZIMA-CAD Sheet Metal workspace showing a sheet with a formed ventilation opening, its Body history, and the sheet-metal command toolbar.

markers.title: Open Sheet Metal tools
markers.body: Click Sheet Metal to show the sheet-metal command set. It is selected in this capture; the right-hand toolbar contains Sheet, Bend, Profile and Form.

markers.title: Read the Body history
markers.body: The green B01 row identifies the active Body. Its history includes initial sheet F01, its Sketch S01 and the later forming operation that creates the opening.

markers.title: Inspect the formed geometry
markers.body: The narrow raised opening is the calculated forming result. The brown planes and coloured axes around it belong to the displayed Body origin.

markers.title: Find the unfolding controls
markers.body: Unbend is the unfold command. Bend Back is directly below it, followed by DXF export. This capture shows the folded model, not an exported flat pattern.

fem.alt: ZIMA-CAD FEM showing a meshed rod, active Body B2, restraint C1, force C2 = 100 N and a von Mises stress scale in MPa.

markers.title: Read the analysis definition
markers.body: B2 is the active analysis Body and B1 is its source. The tree under B2 lists restraint C1 and force C2.

markers.title: Check loads and restraints
markers.body: The yellow markers show C2 = 100 N and restraint C1 with UX=0, UY=0, UZ=0. These are the loads and restraints of this linear-statics example.

markers.title: Read the result scale
markers.body: The Von Mises stress [MPa] legend shows element-average stress. Blue marks the lower end and red the upper end; the displayed maximum is approximately 0.93978 MPa.

markers.title: Choose a result display
markers.body: Choose Displacement [mm] or Von Mises stress [MPa] on the right. Show deformation toggles result visibility. The lower-left label reports magnification ×1 and a static result.

cam.alt: ZIMA-CAD Generic NC program inspector with a selected linear motion, motion stepping controls, stock-result toggle, and the corresponding tool position over a workpiece.

markers.title: Select a motion
markers.body: Click a motion row to show its tool position. Row 8, LINEAR X0 Y-2 Z2, is selected here. The header identifies this as generic NC that requires controller postprocessing.

markers.title: Step through the program
markers.body: Next motion and Previous motion move between motions. The slider on their right interpolates the tool position within the selected motion; it does not scan the whole program.

markers.title: Show calculated remaining stock
markers.body: Toggle Show calculated remaining stock to inspect the calculated remaining stock. The box is unchecked in this screenshot.

markers.title: Relate the program to the view
markers.body: The model view places the displayed tool over the workpiece at the selected program motion. Keep this view and the selected NC row together when checking the path.

getting-started.alt: ZIMA-CAD New Document dialog with Part selected, the name model, the Modeling environment, and OK and Cancel.

markers.title: Name the document
markers.body: Enter the document name in File name. This example uses model, a user-defined name.

markers.title: Choose a Part
markers.body: Select Part for a Part document. Assembly creates an Assembly and Drawing creates a Drawing; their radio buttons are below.

markers.title: Select the Part environment
markers.body: Choose the Part environment beside Part. Modeling is selected here for ordinary Part modeling.

markers.title: Create the selected document
markers.body: Click OK after checking the name, document type and environment. This screenshot shows the creation dialog before a document has been created.

sweep.alt: ZIMA-CAD initial 2D Sweep Properties dialog with XY selected, the Path Sketch button, two profile stations and empty placement references.

markers.title: Choose the path plane
markers.body: Click XY, XZ or YZ to choose the container plane for the path sketch. XY is selected in this capture.

markers.title: Define the path sketch
markers.body: Click Path sketch… to edit the sweep path. The placement reference table above is empty in this initial definition.

markers.title: Define station profiles
markers.body: Click Sketch in the station row to edit its profile. The first row is 1 — start and the second is 1 — end. Both currently request the first profile with Fill in the first profile.

markers.title: Confirm a complete sweep
markers.body: After defining the path and required profiles, click OK to validate and calculate the sweep. Cancel discards pending changes. This capture shows setup controls, not a calculated sweep result.

assembly.alt: ZIMA-CAD Component Properties in an Assembly, showing a source Part, three paired origin planes at zero offset, independent inspection eyes and zero remaining degrees of freedom.

markers.title: Check the source Part
markers.body: The Source field identifies component-reference.prtz as this occurrence’s source. The Assembly tree contains two occurrences of that Part.

markers.title: Read the placement pairs
markers.body: The This part and Target columns pair the component and target references. XY, YZ and XZ are paired here, each with the Face type and a 0,000 mm offset.

markers.title: Inspect each reference independently
markers.body: Click the eye under Show part to inspect the component reference, or the neighbouring eye under Show target to inspect the target reference.

markers.title: Check the remaining freedom
markers.body: Remaining degrees of freedom: 0 reports no remaining degrees of freedom for these three plane pairs. Click OK at the lower right to confirm the pending placement; Cancel discards its changes.

drawings.alt: ZIMA-CAD Drawing View Properties showing the source model, view label rows, custom orientation, visible-edge mode, scale 0.500 and sheet position.

markers.title: Choose the source model
markers.body: Open Source to select the view source, or click File to choose a file. The current source is Drawing source — Native (generic).

markers.title: Set the projection orientation
markers.body: Open Standard view: to choose a base view. Custom orientation is selected here, with horizontal 17°, vertical −23° and in-plane 31° angles in the fields below.

markers.title: Set the drawing scale
markers.body: The Scale: selector is Custom and Value is 0,500, corresponding to the M1:2 label above. The X and Y fields below position the view on the sheet in millimetres.

markers.title: Confirm the view properties
markers.body: Click OK to confirm the view settings or Cancel to discard pending changes. This capture shows the view definition dialog; the projected sheet geometry is outside the screenshot.

render.alt: ZIMA-CAD spotlight Properties in a Render Body, showing the selected light in the tree, placement controls, white colour, 1000 lm luminous flux and a 45-degree cone with its scene glyph.

markers.title: Identify the scene light
markers.body: Spotlight 1 is selected under Render Body 1, alongside Camera 1 and Sun 1. The open Properties edit the spotlight.

markers.title: Set colour and luminous flux
markers.body: Edit Color (#RRGGBB) for the light colour and Luminous power for luminous flux. This example uses #ffffff and 1000 lm, with Light enabled checked.

markers.title: Set the spotlight cone
markers.body: Edit Cone angle to change the cone angle; it reads 45° here. Light radius is 5 mm and Edge softness is 0,25 in the neighbouring fields.

markers.title: Relate the light to the scene
markers.body: The cyan cone in the model view is the spotlight glyph. Show marker in View is checked in the dialog. Click OK at the bottom right to confirm the pending light settings.
